parts.problem_md:
Rationalise the denominator of  $\frac{4}{7-\sqrt{5}}$

Show each stage of your working.

Give your answer in the form $a+b\sqrt{5}$ where $a$ and $b$ are fractions in their simplest forms.
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> Rationalising the denominator is the process of eliminating radicals (like square roots/surds) from the denominator of a fraction.
> 
> The process involves multiplying the fraction by the value of 1 using suitable expressions.

> *Use the inverse operation of the denominator to select  an expression to multiply the numerator and denominator by*

*The inverse operation of *$7-\sqrt{5}$* is *$7+\sqrt{5}$

> *Multiplying the fraction by *$\frac{7+\sqrt{5}}{7+\sqrt{5}}$*will eliminate the surd from the denominator*

`fraction numerator 4 over denominator open parentheses 7 minus square root of 5 close parentheses end fraction cross times fraction numerator open parentheses 7 plus square root of 5 close parentheses over denominator open parentheses 7 plus square root of 5 close parentheses end fraction`

**[M1]**

> *Multiply the fractions, expand the double brackets on the denominator and apply the laws of surds*

`fraction numerator 4 open parentheses 7 plus square root of 5 close parentheses over denominator open parentheses 7 minus square root of 5 close parentheses open parentheses 7 plus square root of 5 close parentheses end fraction equals fraction numerator 28 plus 4 square root of 5 over denominator 49 minus 7 square root of 5 plus 7 square root of 5 minus square root of 25 end fraction`

**[M1]**

> *Simplify terms*

$\frac{28+4\sqrt{5}}{49-5}=\frac{28+4\sqrt{5}}{44}$

> *Divide each term by the highest common factor (HCF) to simplify the fraction, in this case the HCF is 4*

$\frac{7+\sqrt{5}}{11}$

> *Leave in the form *$a+b\sqrt{5}$* by separating the terms in the numerator each with a denominator of 11*

$\frac{7}{11}+\frac{1}{11}\sqrt{5}$

**[A1]**
